Upcoming National Weather Service updates and real-time observations from Buckley Space Force Base will determine whether the high settles in the 96–97 °F range favored by traders or edges into the lower-probability 98–99 °F bin.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Marine layer and persistent onshore flow from the Pacific are anchoring San Francisco’s August 6 high near the climatological normal of ~70 °F.** National Weather Service forecasts issued early on the 6th call for morning marine stratus giving way to gradual clearing, with a high of 72 °F downtown and slightly warmer readings (~76 °F) at SFO; light west-southwest winds of 6–14 mph limit afternoon heating.  

These conditions explain the market’s tight clustering around 70–73 °F (combined >65 % implied probability). The 68–69 °F bin retains meaningful support because a thicker or slower-dissipating marine layer remains possible, while probabilities drop sharply above 74 °F absent a stronger offshore component or anomalous warming. Historical early-August maxima average 69–71 °F, so the current distribution reflects only modest day-to-day variability rather than any extreme deviation from baseline coastal cooling.  

Traders will watch the next NWS update and real-time observations for any shift in the depth or timing of the marine layer, which remains the dominant control on today’s peak temperature.

Winter climatology in Wellington supports this range: long-term August daytime maxima average near 12°C, with typical highs between 10–14°C under southerly or westerly flows. Current synoptic setup—a departing ridge followed by a Tasman Sea front—favors modest daytime warming without strong northerly advection that could push readings to 15°C or higher. Model consensus and the absence of significant warm-air advection keep 14°C at just 13.5% while 12°C holds secondary support at 20%.

Traders appear to weight the MetService guidance and ensemble outputs heavily, with probabilities tightly clustered around the 12–14°C band that matches both forecast guidance and historical variability for early August. Upcoming model runs and any overnight updates to the official forecast remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift these market-implied odds.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the Pakistan Meteorological Department and international forecasts points to peak daytime temperatures in Karachi hovering near 33–34°C on August 8, with market-implied odds of 43.5% for 34°C and 37.5% for 33°C reflecting traders’ weighting of modest uncertainty. Persistent monsoon moisture, variable cloud cover, and sea-breeze effects are moderating maximums below seasonal norms of around 32–33°C, while any reduction in convective activity could allow brief warming toward 35°C. Historical August variability and the short two-day forecast horizon amplify sensitivity to the next PMD and global model updates, keeping probabilities tightly clustered.
